Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0036", "row_sha256": "e9ec5ba3deccb56aee6a446020e27705f609d7a3e48e112e2788fcb4a7c14a8e", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
lowering this into a usable bakery order form is what i need, not a menu flyer or a description of the shop. Please write a printable order form for Juniper Lane Bakery in Bellwether. It will be handed to customers at the counter and can also be filled in while a staff member takes an order by phone. keep it clear enough to complete by hand. There is a cloud folder with some old pictures and drafts, but do not open cloud links. The facts in this note are the information to use. You may arrange them into a sensible form and use headings, checkboxes, and short labels.

The bakery is at 18 Alder Street, Bellwether, and the phone is (555) 014-8832. Customers can write to orders@juniperlanebakery.example if they need to ask something before ordering. The shop is open Tuesday through Saturday from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. Orders are picked up at the bakery; there is no delivery service. Pickup times are Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., so the form should let somebody write a pickup date and a time in that window. We are closed Sunday and Monday. The pickup time is when they collect the order, not when they want to place it. Please make the date and time fields easy to find, because we have had people write a party date in the pickup spot.

We take requests for celebration cakes, cupcakes, and pastry boxes. A round cake comes in 6-inch for $28 or 8-inch for $38, and there is a 9-by-13-inch sheet cake for $42. The customer can select vanilla, chocolate, or lemon cake. Buttercream choices are vanilla, chocolate, or lemon; it is frosting, not a cake flavor choice, so keep those separate. A cake can have an inscription, with no more than 30 characters. Ask the customer to write the exact wording, rather than a general message like “something cheerful.” They may request frosting colors too, but those requests are subject to what the bakery can prepare, so don’t make the form promise that every color is available.

Cupcakes are sold by the dozen for $24, in vanilla, chocolate, or lemon. A customer can request one flavor for the dozen, not a mix. Pastry boxes are $18 for six pieces or $34 for twelve. The box can be assorted; there is no need to list individual pastry types because the selection changes. Those are the prices currently used, and the order form should show each price beside the relevant choice. It needs to give the person room to mark quantities without making it look as if a cake size and a cupcake dozen are the same product. The form is for these listed items only, not for custom products that aren’t described here.

Please include a space for the customer's name and a phone number we can use about the order. An email field is useful but optional. Staff need a line for the date the order is taken, as well as a separate pickup date and pickup time. The order date is not the date the customer needs the baked goods. It is fine to have an order-details area for cake size, cake flavor, frosting, inscription, and color request, plus separate places for cupcake quantity and flavor and pastry-box quantity. A customer might order more than one kind of item, so don’t make the whole form force them to pick just one category. There should be enough room to write details, but the page should still be a single printable page.

For timing, celebration cakes need at least five calendar days of notice and pastry boxes need at least two calendar days. Cupcakes need two calendar days too. The form should ask when an order is needed without suggesting that an order inside those notice periods is automatically accepted. If the date requested is too soon, staff will need to speak with the customer. Don’t add an approval or confirmation statement; filling in this paper is a request, and staff call to confirm whether they can take it. It should be possible to note a phone conversation, but there is no online checkout and no need for card-number fields.

There is one food-safety detail that should be visible and not buried in tiny print: the bakery handles wheat, eggs, milk, and soy in a shared kitchen. We can’t guarantee an item is free of cross-contact with those ingredients. Include a short note about that, and a place where the customer can tell us about an allergy or other food concern. That space is for them to tell us, not a promise that we can make a safe substitute. Please don’t add claims about gluten-free, nut-free, vegan, or other options because those aren’t part of the details I have.

For the payment part, customers pay when they pick up the order, using cash or a card. No deposit information was given, so don’t invent one. The order form can have a simple payment note and a staff-use line to mark cash or card at pickup, but it should not ask for payment details in advance. The shop’s usual pickup window and closure days should be shown clearly enough that the customer doesn’t ask for Sunday pickup by mistake. This is a paper form for the actual bakery counter, not a web form, and it doesn’t need a place to upload anything.

A small note from the owner was, “I want people to know what they’re asking for, and I want our staff to be able to read it later.” Please make the finished request form calm and practical rather than decorative. No need for a slogan, promotional copy, or a long explanation of the bakery. Include the bakery name and contact details so a loose page can still be identified. Organize the choices so a customer can complete only the relevant parts if ordering one item, while still allowing a combination of cakes, cupcakes, and pastry boxes on the same sheet. Keep all listed prices, lead times, available pickup hours, and product choices as stated here.", "output": "Create a clear, printable, single-page order form for Juniper Lane Bakery in Bellwether. The form will be used at the counter and by staff taking orders over the phone. Make it practical and easy to complete by hand, with space for customers to order one or more product types on the same sheet. Use headings, checkboxes, and short labels where useful. Include the bakery name and contact information so a loose page can be identified. You may organize the details below into a sensible form. Do not open cloud links; use the information in this request.

**Bakery and pickup details**
- Juniper Lane Bakery, 18 Alder Street, Bellwether
- Phone: (555) 014-8832
- Email: orders@juniperlanebakery.example
- Shop hours: Tuesday through Saturday, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m.
- Pickup is at the bakery, Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. There is no delivery service, and the bakery is closed Sunday and Monday.

Provide distinct fields for the date the order is taken and the pickup date and time. Make clear that pickup time means when the customer will collect the order, not when they place it. Do not imply Sunday or Monday pickup is available.

**Products and prices**
- Celebration cakes: 6-inch round, $28; 8-inch round, $38; 9-by-13-inch sheet, $42. Cake flavors: vanilla, chocolate, or lemon. Buttercream flavors: vanilla, chocolate, or lemon. Keep cake flavor and frosting choices separate. Include space for an exact cake inscription of no more than 30 characters and an optional frosting-color request. Color requests are subject to what the bakery can prepare; do not promise that every color is available.
- Cupcakes: $24 per dozen, in vanilla, chocolate, or lemon. Each dozen has one flavor; do not offer a mixed dozen.
- Pastry boxes: $18 for six pieces or $34 for twelve. The box may be assorted, and individual pastry types should not be listed because the selection changes.

Show each price beside its product choice. Make quantities easy to mark, and keep the cake, cupcake, and pastry-box options distinct. Include only these listed products; do not add custom products.

**Customer and order information**
Include fields for the customer’s name and phone number, plus an optional email address. Allow room to record cake size, cake flavor, buttercream, inscription, and color request, as well as cupcake quantity and flavor and pastry-box quantity. Customers may order multiple product types, but should be able to complete only the relevant sections. Leave enough room for written details while keeping the form to one printable page.

**Timing and confirmation**
Celebration cakes require at least five calendar days’ notice. Cupcakes and pastry boxes each require at least two calendar days’ notice. Ask for the requested pickup date without suggesting that an order placed inside those notice periods is automatically accepted. If the requested date is too soon, staff need to speak with the customer. This paper form is a request, not confirmation; staff call to confirm whether they can take the order. Do not add an approval or confirmation statement. A staff member may note a phone conversation. There is no online checkout, and the form should not request card numbers.

**Food-safety note**
Make this information visible: the bakery handles wheat, eggs, milk, and soy in a shared kitchen and cannot guarantee an item is free of cross-contact with those ingredients. Include a short note and space for the customer to mention an allergy or other food concern. Do not imply that the bakery can provide a safe substitute or add claims about gluten-free, nut-free, vegan, or other options.

**Payment and presentation**
Customers pay at pickup by cash or card. Include a simple payment note and a staff-use line to mark cash or card at pickup. Do not invent a deposit or request advance payment details. Keep the form calm and practical, not decorative. Do not add a slogan, promotional copy, or a long description of the bakery. The owner’s goal is: “I want people to know what they’re asking for, and I want our staff to be able to read it later.”"}]
